geometry_edits.rationale: The current cantilever is too sealed and singular; splitting the dominant mass is the most direct way to create a ground threshold and restore neighborhood-living publicness.
Align the split with the long axis so the resulting void reads as a meaningful sectional seam instead of a random notch.
Keep a bridge condition so the edited mass remains one dominant hierarchy rather than two unrelated pieces.
Tune the gap to expose a legible public void without over-fragmenting the building.
Add a courtyard macro around the dominant mass to make the open-space figure explicit and programmatic.
Promote the courtyard-wrapped mass so the public void remains in the ancestry of the final root.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the pure cantilever dominance with a clearer split-wing logic so the mass can register a ground-facing threshold and a more legible public void.
Split along the long direction to preserve a dominant anchor while opening a clearer central/public seam.
Allow a controlled reconnecting bridge so the split remains one hierarchy rather than two detached fragments.
Moderate gap to create a readable public/entry void without collapsing the mass into fragments.
Add a support void operation to produce a more explicit usable courtyard/public recess tied to the ground plane.
Use a bounded courtyard margin to keep the void public but still integrated with the compact site.

rationale: The candidate reads as a small stepped/cantilevered object with some formal continuity, but the four views show a weak and semantically unclear ground response to the verified access edge. The blue frontage is treated more as an external line than a legible entry seam, court, or undercut, so the public threshold invariant is not satisfied. The parcel is generally contained, and the form is coherent across views, but it is close to a generic stacked mass with a top-heavy profile rather than a clear neighborhood-living building with active ground and public void logic. The stepped silhouette is acceptable as a massing move, yet here it behaves more like arbitrary tiering than a capacity-bearing inhabited section. The result is not visually contradictory, but program fit is too weak to hard-pass: it lacks a convincing mixed-use ground, entry zone, or sectional public-space relationship. The best transferable correction from the counterfactual reference is to privilege a continuous sectional carve/terrace or courtyard-oriented public spine rather than adding more fragmented stepbacks.
